recommendation.rationale: Comment and value preservation are central to this migrator. Python can use a maintained TOML library that preserves comments, then rely on standard-library code for validation and atomic replacement. Veritas has atomic file replacement and packaging, but the supplied capabilities do not include TOML parsing; using its Python bridge would add managed interpreter, dependency, and packaging setup for the same TOML library. No comparative results support a performance or size claim.
conditions: If the app must run without relying on any installed Python runtime, Veritas becomes more attractive because its package can include its runtime and a managed Python environment for the bridge.
If a suitable comment-preserving TOML library is unavailable in the shared offline wheelhouse, reassess the Python approach against Veritas’s managed bridge path.
If later measurements show the Veritas bridge package meets relocation requirements with materially lower setup cost or package size, reconsider Veritas.
